scope: Two new biological year profiles: Feldhase and Dachs. Eighteen distinct knowledge blocks, 24 month views and four fields per view. Targeted correction of the existing badger birth paragraph only; no full review of all older species or the app.
method: Read named specialist organizations against each concrete block. Different URLs under the Bavarian ministry were counted as one organization. Monthly bands are editorial orientation, not absolute individual dates. Technical tests check structure and links, not factual certification.

supports: Approximately 42–43-day gestation; young born furred and seeing but still suckled
Broad plant diet and year-round edges
Reproduction February–October; about 42 days, seeing/furred young still suckled
Plant diet and harvest-related changes in food and cover
Field margins, hedges and fallow sites
Body/ear/fur identification and lighter winter coat
Sasse, loose pairing groups, young born furred and seeing after about 42 days
Face mask, grey back, short dark legs
Broad pairing January–October, embryonic delay, births late February–early April
Ground-based animal and plant foods including fallen fruit and maize
Births January–March in burrows, emerging after weeks
Postpartum pairing and delay until winter development
Winter rest can be interrupted for feeding
Winter-resting animals can be intermittently active and seek food; distinction from true hibernation

qualifications.issue: Hare pairing and reproduction season are given differently
qualifications.evidence: DJV/WFS December or January–August pairing versus LfL February–October reproduction.
qualifications.handling: Pairing and the longer birth/upbringing season are explicitly separated; no universal last birth date. November is grouped with season transition, not claimed as a regular birth month.

qualifications.evidence: DWT January–March, DJV late February–early April, Bavaria February/March.
qualifications.handling: Use late winter/early spring and show the exact difference in the note. A January birth is a possible edge case, not excluded by the main February–April teaching band.

qualifications.evidence: Bavarian species page says metabolism remains unchanged; DWT species page describes a strong reduction while its winter article qualifies reduction as less drastic than true hibernation.
qualifications.handling: Do not publish numeric or absolute metabolic statements. Explain only independently agreed winter rest with possible activity/feeding interruptions.
Reused verified real portraits illustrate species only. They are not evidence for the selected month, sex, age, birth, diet intake or health.
